validity.researcher_notes: TEST APPLIED: this cohort's rows were identified visually off the GASCO national-grid MAP on printed p.35 of the EGAS Annual Report 2018, so a full-text-search miss is not evidence against the citation (per the scope brief); I both (a) read the report's own completed/under-construction project TEXT TABLES directly and (b) extracted and visually read the MAP IMAGE on that page, rather than relying on the worklist's automated substring check. FINDING 1 (automated check is a false positive, not real evidence): the worklist recorded 'Length [ref]'/'Diameter [ref]' as '200 + expected content present' for the current ref (egyptoil-gas.com EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf). I downloaded the 22MB PDF and ran pdftotext myself: the literal strings '165' and 'Damietta/Idku'/'Damietta-Idku' do NOT appear anywhere in the extracted prose (the report's own COMPLETED/UNDER-CONSTRUCTION pipeline tables list different, differently-named/sized lines only, e.g. 'Algameel/Damietta pipeline 50km-42"' and 'Ezdwaj Edku/Abu Houmas pipeline 30km-42"' -- neither is this row). url_verifier.verify_url does not parse PDFs; it substring-matches requests.get(url).text against the raw PDF bytes, so a bare numeral like '165' can match binary/compressed stream data with zero relation to visible content -- this is the same 'large PDF, extractor unreliable' failure family the script's own docstring already warns about, just manifesting as a false PASS instead of a false FAIL here. This is a general defect worth the orchestrator's attention (out of scope for me to patch mid-batch), but it does not change my verdict because I verified the real content independently below. FINDING 2 (real map evidence, exact match): PDF page 19 (printed page 35, confirmed by the page-bottom folio '35' in the extracted text and by a 200-ppi CMYK raster embedded on that page, matching the map-page signature already documented for this cohort) carries GASCO's 'NATIONAL GAS GRID' wall map. I extracted the embedded map image directly (pdfimages) and read it at full resolution: it shows a label reading exactly '32" 165 k.m' positioned on the coastal strip immediately beside the 'L N G Idku' / 'Nedoco' facility labels, i.e. at the Idku end of the coastal corridor toward Damietta -- an EXACT match to both the sheet's Diameter (32in) and Length (165km). The backbone line running through that stretch (via Burullus PS, Abu Madi, toward the Damietta/El-Tina cluster) is drawn in the map's GREEN line style, which its own legend defines as 'EXISTING P/L' (as opposed to the red 'UNDER CONS. P/L' lines visible elsewhere on the same map, e.g. near Abu Qir/W.D.G. Complex) -- corroborating Status=operating by the same map. CAVEAT: unlike some of this map's labels (e.g. 'Repco Gas 42"40km' -> visibly leadered to 'Wastany'), the '32"165km' label has no clearly drawn leader line to a single specific route in my extraction, so I cannot rule out with certainty that it labels an adjacent offshore-field gathering line into Idku rather than this exact onshore Idku-Damietta trunk -- I flag this rather than overclaiming a clean match (this is the same discipline that caught a genuine mislabel elsewhere in this cohort, per the country note's P8051/42in-vs-32in mix-up). FINDING 3 (independent, non-EGAS-report corroboration of EXISTENCE): Petroleum Magazine (petro-mag.org), Nov 2025 special issue -- a wholly separate 2025 trade-magazine PDF, unrelated to and much later than the 2018 EGAS report -- states in its GASCO security-hardening section: 'تركيب وتشغيل كاميرات المراقبة بغرفة (12) خط إدكو/دمياط' ('installation and operation of monitoring cameras at chamber (12), the Edku/Damietta line'), naming an operational GASCO valve chamber on a named 'Edku/Damietta' line as of the 2025 security-upgrade programme. url_verifier FAILs the Arabic substrings ('إدكو'/'دمياط' both 'missing expected') against this URL -- this is the documented ligature-encoded-Arabic-PDF false-negative family in the verifier's own docstring ('the contains-value check can't read contiguous Arabic; verify with pdftotext before discarding'); I downloaded the PDF and confirmed with pdftotext -enc UTF-8 that the exact phrase appears at that location (line ~2615 of the extraction), so I am citing it per that documented exception, not overriding rule 3 blind. This second, independent document gives EXISTENCE/naming support (a real, currently-monitored 'Idku/Damietta' GASCO line) but not the km/diameter figures, so overall tier is medium rather than high: one document (EGAS map) carries the value with a leader-line ambiguity caveat, the other (Petroleum Magazine) is a clean independent existence confirmation without the spec numbers. CLASSIFICATION: transmission/Gas is consistent with this being part of GASCO's national gas-grid backbone connecting two major governorate/LNG hubs (Damietta, Idku), not a gathering/feeder spur -- no reclassification warranted. DUPLICATE CROSS-CHECK (roster item, see separate validity entry below) and LOCATION: StartLocation is currently blank in the sheet (only StartState/Province='Damietta' is populated); Wikipedia's 'SEGAS LNG' article independently places that Damietta-side gas/LNG hub in 'Damietta, Egypt', but that does not add precision beyond what StartState/Province already records (and the specific pipeline tie-in point, as opposed to the SEGAS plant itself, is not established by any source I found), so I am leaving StartLocation unfilled rather than fabricating a more specific point.

validity.recommendation: No merge. If P8010 is later confirmed as a real 42in/121km Gamasa-Edku line, note the shared Edku/Idku endpoint and adjacent corridor in both rows' ResearcherNotes, but keep them as two separate physical assets.
validity.researcher_notes: Roster watchlist item: 'P8010 Gamasa-Edku vs P8027 Damietta-Idku -- Edku and Idku are the same place. Check.' Confirmed Edku/Idku is one town (إدكو, Beheira governorate; both English spellings are used interchangeably across sources for the same LNG hub). However P8027 (Damietta start, 32in, 165km, operating) and P8010 (Gamasa start, 42in, 121km, proposed) differ on diameter, origin town, length and status -- per the standing heuristic (different diameter = usually two real parallel lines, not a duplicate) this is not a duplicate call, and I found no source describing a single line that is alternately called 'Damietta-Idku' and 'Gamasa-Edku'. Cross-cutting note for the reviewer, not a P8027 defect: while researching P8027 I found the Petroleum Magazine (Nov 2025) PDF's 'future projects' list for GASCO's national grid states verbatim 'إنشاء خط ازدواج جمصة – إدكو قطر 42 بوصة بطول 121كم' ('establish a duplication line Gamasa-Edku, 42in diameter, 121km') -- an exact match to P8010's own recorded spec (42in/121km) as a currently-proposed project, which appears to directly contradict/resolve P8010's own already-staged 'existence concern' shard (which found no independent source for a Gamasa-Edku line at all). I am flagging this for whoever reconciles the two shards rather than editing P8010.json myself, since P8010 is outside my assigned row.

summary: P8027 CONFIRMED (caveat): Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length(165km)/Diameter(32in) all corroborated by the GASCO national-grid MAP image on the cited EGAS 2018 report's page 35 (an exact '32"165km' label at Idku, green=existing line) plus an independent 2025 Petroleum Magazine mention of an operational 'Edku/Damietta' line -- the worklist's automated Length/Diameter 'content present' pass on that PDF is itself a false positive (verifier doesn't parse PDFs) but the real map evidence holds up; no existence/classification/duplicate concern, though the map label's leader-line attribution is not 100% unambiguous. UNRESOLVED: StartLocation left blank (no source pins a more specific tie-in point than 'Damietta'); also surfaced but not staged here -- new evidence (Petroleum Magazine future-projects list) that may resolve P8010's already-staged existence concern in P8010's favor.
